name: Creamy Tuscan Pork Chops

fit.note: Clears all conditions (400-650 cal, <=35g carbs, no seafood, skillet weigh-and-divide scales to 14). NOT-FIT does not apply; this is a pure duplicate ruling.

reason: Same dinner as the catalog's Marry Me Pork Chops over Pasta: identical sauce (pork-chops + heavy-cream + chicken-broth + parmesan + garlic + sun-dried-tomatoes); the candidate only adds a handful of spinach and drops the starch base. 'Marry Me' and 'Creamy Tuscan' are the canonical name-different-dish-same pair (both are the sun-dried-tomato parmesan cream chop). Protein + sauce family + skillet method all match; only the starch base differs, which does not make it a genuinely different plate.
secondary_neighbors: creamy-mushroom-pork-chops-over-mashed-potatoes (NOT a dupe - mushroom cream sauce, distinct flavor family)
creamy-pork-tenderloin-tagliatelle (NOT a dupe - tenderloin + mushroom/bacon cream over pasta)
cross_protein_collisions: creamy-tuscan-chicken-skillet - ACCEPTED this run in the chicken lane; structurally the same Tuscan sun-dried-tomato cream dish, chicken vs pork. Decider should confirm the run isn't shipping the same Tuscan cream plate across two proteins.
catalog slow-cooker-tuscan-chicken-pasta and chicken-florentine (spinach + parmesan cream) are the chicken-side relatives of this sauce family.
Any turkey/beef 'Marry Me' or 'Tuscan' cream cutlet in another selector's pool would be the same dish - flagging for the cross-protein merge pass.
